answer: One concrete mechanism: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because lantern only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, grove is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any canyon approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
